children: By Chris Cumming
Alternative-investment manager Siguler Guff & Co. amassed its largest fund yet to back some of private-equity's smallest deals.
The Fund

The New York firm raised $3 billion for Siguler Guff Small Buyout Opportunities Fund VI, including $700 million across separately managed accounts, it plans to announce Thursday. The fundraising haul surpassed both the firm's $2.2 billion target and the $1.97 billion that it raised for its predecessor, which closed in 2022.

Institutions that backed the vehicle include the Cincinnati Retirement System, the Vermont Pension Investment Commission, the Municipal Fire & Police Retirement System of Iowa and the Foundation of California State University, Monterey Bay, according to public filings and data-tracking firm PitchBook.
The Strategy

With $18.4 billion under management, Siguler Giff says it is one of the most active investors in small and lower-midmarket companies in the U.S. It has committed more than $10 billion in over 1000 companies through the small-business strategy since launching it in 2006.

The strategy invests about half its capital in funds managed by small, specialist private-equity firms, and half directly in deals, said Kevin Kester, a Siguler Guff partner who co-leads the small-business strategy, alongside Partner Jonathan Wilson.

Siguler Guff's small buyout strategy looks for family- or founder-led companies with less than $200 million in annual revenue and typically $10 million to $30 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.
Kester calls this area "a permanent inefficiency in the market," with far less private-equity money chasing deals than in the midmarket or higher.

The firm looks to invest with private-equity firms that have deep sector experience and "can source deals in less competitive ways" than through typical bank auctions, said Kester. It generally commits to funds below $500 million in size, including first-time funds.

This Siguler Guff strategy has been a significant early backer to firms including Mountaingate Capital in Denver, Pennsylvania-based Guardian Capital Partners, healthcare specialist NaviMed Capital and consumer-products-focused Encore Consumer Capital.
So far the firm has deployed roughly half of the capital raised for Fund VI, with firms including Guardian Capital and Encore Consumer, Kester said.

Siguler Guff was formed in 1991 as part of the investment bank PaineWebber and went independent in 1995. Along with its small-business private-equity strategy, the firm also manages credit, emerging-markets, real estate and energy strategies.
The Context

Private-equity fundraising continues to struggle in 2026, due to the industry's backlog of unsold companies and declining commitments by institutions that have long been the industry's biggest backers.

Globally, private-capital funds are on pace for the fifth consecutive annual decline since hitting their peak of about $1.9 trillion in 2021, according to PitchBook. Through June, private funds raised about $658 billion, a slower pace than last year, when they gathered $1.47 trillion over the full 12 months.

Although Siguler Guff's fund beat its target, Kester said this is "a much more challenging environment than when we raised our previous fund," because investors have cut back their allocations to private equity.
He said the fundraise succeeded, however, in part because the vehicle is an efficient way to invest in an attractive part of the market that can be difficult for larger institutions to access.
